mechanism.name: Yang-He (2012) Section 4.2 Models 1-4: fixed-query conditional 0.95 quantile

generation_equations.label: Common covariate law, Section 4.2 p.1114
generation_equations.expression: X ~ chi-square(df=2); Z = 2B, B ~ Bernoulli(0.5); X, Z, e mutually independent.

generation_equations.label: Model 2, p.1114
generation_equations.expression: Y=X+Z+e; log(e)~Normal(mean=0, variance=1); e is not centered.

generation_equations.label: Model 4, p.1114
generation_equations.expression: Y=X+Z+(1+X/2)e; log(e)~Normal(mean=0, variance=1); e is not centered.

generation_equations.label: Derived target adaptation
generation_equations.expression: theta_m=2+s_m(2)q_e(0.95), with s_1=s_2=1, s_3(x)=s_4(x)=1+x/2; q_normal(tau)=2 Phi^{-1}(tau), q_lognormal(tau)=exp(Phi^{-1}(tau)).

sampling.unit: One synthetic observation (X,Z,Y); n is the number of rows.
sampling.dependence: iid across rows; X, Z, e mutually independent before constructing Y; Y depends on X and Z through the declared law.
sampling.within_unit_dependence: Primitive X,Z,e independent; Z=2B deterministic; G=log(e) for Models2/4; Y depends on X,Z,e. Heteroscedastic scaled noise s(X)e is not independent of X.
sampling.between_unit_dependence: iid synthetic rows; no shared random effects, clusters, panels or network structure.

assumptions: Independent identically distributed observed rows (X,Z,Y), as in the random-sample framework of Section 2; within each row X, Z and e are mutually independent as explicitly stated on p.1114.
Complete observation of X,Z,Y; n denotes the number of iid rows. No missingness, clustering, panel or network dependence is introduced.
The declared conditional location-scale law defines a continuous version at X=2 despite P(X=2)=0; the query lies inside the continuous X support and Z=0 has probability 0.5.
The source scale is 1 or 1+X/2, strictly positive on X>=0. Conditional density is continuous and positive at the queried 0.95 quantile, so this quantile is unique.

For inference using a quantile-regression estimator, correct conditional-quantile specification and a nondegenerate design are relevant. Both covariates are active and E[(1,X,Z)(1,X,Z)^T] is positive definite.

The source Assumption 3.2 requires bounded covariate support, but the simulation X~chi-square(2) is unbounded. Preserve the simulation law, do not assert all BEL theorem conditions or finite-sample coverage. Prior and EL feasibility assumptions are method-specific and are not certified here.
Noncausal QDI functional: no intervention, treatment exchangeability, mediation, cross-world or interference assumptions are imposed.

properties.notes: Two observed covariates X and Z, both active; the intercept is not a covariate column. This is low-dimensional (p=2; source n=100, smoke n=128). Q_tau=x+z+s(x)q_e(tau) is affine in observed covariates for all models, with no X*Z term. In Models 3-4, (X/2)e is a covariate-noise product inducing heteroscedasticity, not an observed-covariate interaction. Models 2/4 use the nonlinear latent transform exp(G), explicitly recorded as non-Gaussian noise; the nonlinear tag here describes the observed-covariate quantile surface, not noise simulation. Var(Y|X,Z)=s(X)^2 Var(e); no padding variables or causal confounding claim.

estimand.name: theta_m = Q_0.95(Y | X=2,Z=0), m=1,2,3,4

adaptations: Retain the four published data-generating laws and all their parameters. Treat Models 1-4 as four scenarios in one mechanism family.
Select only tau=0.95 from the original joint levels 0.9, 0.925, 0.95 and target a scalar conditional quantile, not the full vector of regression coefficients.
Replace the original sample-dependent adjusted intercept at (sample mean X,0) with the fixed query (X,Z)=(2,0), where 2=E[X]. This is a target adaptation, not a reported source-paper truth.
Use local Python RNG and CPU smoke n=128, seed=1729; original simulations use n=100 and 500 samples. No claim to replicate the original random stream, estimator MSE, priors or MCMC computations.
